profiles.meeting_scenario: Two researchers in an ML lab are holding a brainstorming meeting to generate follow-up project ideas building on a recent paper about neural architecture search for spiking neural networks. The lab wants a workshop submission in six weeks that extends the paper's initialization-based search idea to a new setting and demonstrates a credible research direction without requiring a full large-scale training campaign. The meeting context is that they have already skimmed the seed paper and now want to brainstorm promising variants around temporal feedback, spike-pattern diversity at initialization, and low-timestep evaluation. The agenda is to identify 2-3 candidate project directions, narrow them to one likely prototype, and sketch what would count as a convincing early result. The expected outcome is an informal agreement on one brainstormed direction, what 'small-scale validation' would look like, and who will draft the first experiment memo.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: Neural architecture search, efficient deep learning, benchmark design
members.background: Maya leads a university ML systems and learning theory lab; her recent work focuses on zero-cost proxies for architecture selection and publishing method papers that generalize across tasks.
members.private_state: She wants a project that looks methodologically novel and portable beyond the exact SNN paper, but she is trying to avoid committing the group to expensive full-scale retraining before they know whether the idea has a workshop-level story.
hidden_assumptions: If they say a direction is 'training-free,' that still allows a lightweight post-search confirmation run of a few epochs because the novelty claim is about the search criterion, not literal zero optimization end-to-end.
A 'temporal task' extension naturally includes static image datasets converted into spike trains with different latency or event encodings, because temporal structure can be induced by the encoder.
When discussing whether a search score is 'predictive,' a rank-level correlation over candidate architectures is the meaningful standard, even if absolute accuracy is noisy.
A 'backward connection' in this context means an inter-layer temporal feedback edge unrolled across timesteps, not a same-timestep recurrent loop that changes simulator stability assumptions.

members.name: Arjun Patel
members.expertise: Spiking neural networks, neuromorphic simulation, event-based vision
members.background: Arjun has spent the last two years implementing SNNs on event-camera benchmarks and profiling timestep/energy tradeoffs; he is the likely first author for the follow-up project.
members.private_state: He wants a project that can be prototyped quickly with the lab's existing SNN codebase and that will look technically credible to SNN reviewers, especially around simulator-faithful temporal dynamics and event-driven data.
hidden_assumptions: If they say a direction is 'training-free,' the whole pitch should avoid any gradient-based training after search, otherwise reviewers will see it as another cheap proxy plus ordinary tuning pipeline.
A 'temporal task' means genuinely time-resolved event streams such as DVS Gesture or N-MNIST, not static images artificially expanded into timesteps by an encoder.

When discussing whether a search score is 'predictive,' it should separate the top few candidates well enough that the best searched architecture remains best after full training, since rank over a broad pool is not practically useful.

A 'backward connection' in SNN architecture search should be implemented as a local recurrent state update compatible with the simulator's discrete-time membrane dynamics, not as arbitrary cross-layer feedback edges carried across unrolled timesteps.
If they say they can do a 'small validation,' that should fit inside the existing event-stream code path and not require rebuilding data preprocessing or surrogate-training infrastructure.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a training-free extension
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both propose a 'training-free search' follow-up
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the architecture ranking itself uses only initialization-time spike statistics, while a short post-search training run is still acceptable to show the selected model is promising.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the entire proof-of-concept should avoid gradient-based training after search and rely on initialization-time or direct simulation evidence only.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In zero-cost NAS conversations, 'training-free' often colloquially refers to the search stage rather than the whole pipeline, so both hear a familiar phrase and assume the other is using the same community shorthand.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the follow-up should test on a 'more temporal benchmark'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a setting where temporal spike structure is present, including static image benchmarks encoded into 5-10 spike timesteps with richer temporal coding schemes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a genuinely temporal event-stream dataset collected over time, such as DVS Gesture, where timing comes from the sensor rather than synthetic encoding.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Within SNN work, both synthetic spike encodings and event-camera streams are casually described as 'temporal,' so the phrase sounds precise enough even though their dataset scope differs.

misalignment_points.topic: What would make the proxy predictive
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the new initialization score should be 'predictive of final performance'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 would consider it successful if the score shows a reasonably strong rank correlation across dozens of sampled architectures and helps prune the search space better than random.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 would consider it successful only if the top architecture or top few selected by the score still come out best after a proper SNN training run on the target benchmark.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both standards are common in NAS discussions and are usually compressed into the same phrase 'predictive,' so the conversation can proceed smoothly without surfacing whether they mean global correlation or top-k fidelity.

misalignment_points.topic: How backward connections would be instantiated
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to brainstorm adding 'backward connections' to the search space
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 imagines searchable feedback edges from higher to lower layers that inject signals at the next timestep in the unrolled computational graph, extending the seed paper's architecture language.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 imagines constrained recurrent updates within the simulator, such as gated residual membrane feedback or layer-local recurrence, because arbitrary cross-layer feedback would complicate stable implementation and fair timing comparisons.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The seed paper itself uses the phrase 'backward connections,' which licenses surface agreement, and both implementations sound like natural operationalizations of the same idea until concrete coding details are discussed later.

turns.inner_thought: We need something that still reads as training-free in the zero-cost NAS sense, but I do not want to box us out of doing a short confirmation run later. The workshop story should be: extend the initialization-based criterion, add richer temporal structure, maybe introduce backward connections as a clean architectural twist, and keep the cost low until we know it is publishable. For temporal structure, I am perfectly happy if that comes from a spike encoder over a handful of timesteps. And if we can frame backward connections as next-timestep feedback edges, that feels methodologically broader than just another SNN engineering tweak.
